_about: The whole world's design map (Dan's painted map traced, v5, approved 2026-10-22) and the Act 1 layout (v10). `world`: coast, islands, zones, routes, rivers, settlements, landmarks in world metres (x east, north is -z). `terrain`: painted mountain, snow, volcanic, forest and moor outlines plus peaks. `act1`: the detailed Act 1 layout in its own local metres; world = local + world.act1Offset. tools/world/bake_world.py turns this file into data/terrain/world.bin (heights and walkable ground in 128 m tiles) and data/terrain/water.json. Re-run it after changing this file.

world._about: Shadowfell world map v5 (2026-10-22): traced from the pixels of Dan's painted map (coast from its sea colour, terrain from its paint, zone borders along his) (dan-world-map.png, 1024x1536 px = 5 m per px, world x=(px-512)*5, z=(py-768)*5). x east, z south (north = -z), metres. Act 1 local + act1Offset = world.

zones.name: Bracken country
zones.mood: Hedged fields, a river town, the Blackwood, the Mere. Where you start, on the north shore of the Great Inlet.

zones.name: The Wrack
zones.mood: The long windswept arm south of the Great Inlet: grey shingle, dune grass bent flat, wrecks. Not named on Dan's map yet.

zones.name: The Kingsfold
zones.mood: Rich farms, mills and orchards east of the Great Inlet; the King's Road runs through. Act 2's Blackhedge trouble spills in from the Sallow Downs at its north-west corner.

zones.name: The Elderholt
zones.mood: The beautiful forest: old beeches, gold light, deer, the King's hunting runs.

zones.name: The Mirefen
zones.mood: Reed marsh and eel water west of the Mere, mist every morning, fowlers and fen folk.

zones.name: Blackwater Sump
zones.mood: Warm black swamp: drowned trees, leeches, a sunken abbey. Where the Mirefen goes bad.

zones.name: The Howe Moors
zones.mood: Heather, peat, standing stones and barrows. The dead stir here.

zones.name: The Witherwood
zones.mood: The Blackwood's dead heart, north of Act 1: grey trees, bells in the branches, a village with its tables still laid.

zones.name: The Scarrow
zones.mood: Iron country east of the Greyspine: scree, mine towns, slag and smoke. The cart's iron came from here.

zones.name: The Grey Fells
zones.mood: High rock and wind below the snow line; the Northwall runs along the top.

zones.name: The Scour
zones.mood: Red-gold desert where great stone ribs arch out of the sand; glassmakers, oases, pearl divers on the coast.

zones.name: Sunder Strand
zones.mood: Dunes, salt pans and wreck-strewn beaches on the warm south coast.

zones.name: The Tanglewild
zones.mood: Jungle on the warm south-west coast: vines over old ruins, rain, parrots, a tree as big as a hill.

zones.name: The Hoarlands
zones.mood: Snow, ice and wind past the Northwall; whalers on the coast, a frozen waterfall.

zones.name: Embercrown
zones.mood: The burning skull at the top of the Greyspine: ash, lava runs, black glass, hot springs.

routes.name: The Greyspine pass
routes.note: East over the Greyspine to Coldforge: the road the cart came over. Shut by the rockslide until Act 2.

routes.name: The King's Road
routes.note: East out of Bracken country round the foot of the Greyspine to the Halfway House.

routes.name: The flooded causeway
routes.note: West from the Mere over the fen to Causeway End.

routes.name: The Throat
routes.note: A gorge north out of the deep Blackwood into the Witherwood, towards the Bellwood.

routes.name: Fishermen's path
routes.note: Round the head of the Great Inlet and out along the Wrack.

routes.name: The old King's Road
routes.note: Off the Wrack and inland to Millbrook.

routes.name: The fen edge
routes.note: North out of the Mirefen onto the moor at Fowler's hut.

routes.name: The corpse way
routes.note: East from Cairnholt into the Witherwood.

routes.name: The moor road
routes.note: Up from the Watch on the Howe to Goatherd's stead.

routes.name: The Pass
routes.note: The great gap in the Greyspine, from the Witherwood over to the Scarrow's prospectors.

routes.name: The fell road
routes.note: North out of the Witherwood up to Ravenscar.

routes.name: The Last Gate
routes.note: The only road through the Northwall, on to Frosthaven.

routes.name: The ash road
routes.note: East along the Northwall to the burning crown.

routes.name: The Deep Run
routes.note: A mine-cart line under the hills from the prospectors' valley to the hot springs.

routes.name: The ore road
routes.note: North from the Halfway House to Eastport.

routes.name: The King's Road south
routes.note: South past Millbrook into the beechwoods.

routes.name: The caravan road
routes.note: South-east to the caravanserai at the edge of the sand.

routes.name: The coast track
routes.note: Down through the woods to the strand.

routes.name: The red canyon
routes.note: A dry canyon from the strand up to the pearl divers.

routes.name: The drowned road
routes.note: West out of the Elderholt into the swamp, to the Sunk Abbey.

routes.name: The root path
routes.note: South from the leech-gatherers into the jungle.

routes.name: Sorrow boat
routes.note: From the Wrack's shingle across Bracken Bay to Port Sorrow.

routes.name: Ore boats
routes.note: Eastport down the east coast to Sunder.

routes.name: The Rime run
routes.note: Frosthaven's whalers east along the ice to the sea cliffs below Embercrown.

settlements.name: Brackenford
settlements.note: River town at the ford, where every character first arrives. See the Act 1 map.

settlements.name: Hedgecote
settlements.note: Farm hamlet: the Ashby/Corrick feud.

settlements.name: Stillwater Staithe
settlements.note: Fishers' hamlet on stilts on the Mere.

settlements.name: Woodcutters' camp
settlements.note: The Blackwood's lit forward camp.

settlements.name: Shingle Hythe
settlements.note: A handful of tarred huts and boats hauled up on the shingle. The boat to Port Sorrow leaves from here, if someone pays.

settlements.name: Gull hut
settlements.note: An old fisherman's hut with a crooked chimney, half buried in shingle. He mends nets and tells lies about the bay.

settlements.name: Frosthaven
settlements.note: Whaling town on the north coast: bone arches, ice in the harbour.

settlements.name: Ice-fishers' huts
settlements.note: Huts on runners out on a frozen lake, holes in the ice.

settlements.name: Last Gate
settlements.note: The fortified gate through the Northwall, the only road into the snow.

settlements.name: Ravenscar
settlements.note: Slate-mining town on a cliff edge, ravens on every roof.

settlements.name: The Watch on the Howe
settlements.note: An old fort facing the barrows, half its garrison gone.

settlements.name: Cairnholt
settlements.note: Peat-cutters' village of turf-roofed houses on the moor.

settlements.name: Gravekeepers' house
settlements.note: Where the keepers of the barrows lived. Recently empty.

settlements.name: Fowler's hut
settlements.note: A wildfowler's hut on a hummock, nets and decoy ducks.

settlements.name: Dunmere
settlements.note: An abandoned village, tables still laid.

settlements.name: Reedcutters' camp
settlements.note: Seasonal camp of reed cutters; bundles stacked like haycocks.

settlements.name: Causeway End
settlements.note: Last dry inn before the fen. They rent stilts.

settlements.name: Fenmouth
settlements.note: Eel-fishing village on the causeway: traps, smokehouses, flat-bottomed punts.

settlements.name: The hot springs
settlements.note: Steam pools and a bathhouse at the end of the ash road. Everyone comes here eventually.

settlements.name: Prospectors' camp
settlements.note: Tents and sluices up a cold valley.

settlements.name: Slagtown
settlements.note: Miners' shanties on the slag heaps.

settlements.name: Coldforge
settlements.note: Iron town of furnaces and pit-heads; where the cart's bar iron was bought. The ironmasters want it back.

settlements.name: Eastport
settlements.note: Ore docks on the east coast where iron ships out.

settlements.name: The Halfway House
settlements.note: Coaching inn on the King's Road, a day east of Brackenford. Gossip from both ends.

settlements.name: Millbrook
settlements.note: Orchards and three mills on one stream; cider and quarrels about water.

settlements.name: Hartwell
settlements.note: Charcoal burners and woodwards in the beechwood; their smoke shows above the trees.

settlements.name: The King's Lodge
settlements.note: The old royal hunting lodge, now an inn with antlers on every wall.

settlements.name: The caravanserai
settlements.note: Walled stopping place where the Kingsfold road meets the sand.

settlements.name: Ribshade
settlements.note: Oasis town built in the shade of one of the great stone ribs.

settlements.name: Glassmakers' camp
settlements.note: Tents at the edge of the glass flats.

settlements.name: Pearl divers' camp
settlements.note: Divers' tents on a white beach below the glass flats.

settlements.name: The salt pans
settlements.note: Salt workers' camp on the flats.

settlements.name: Shell Cove
settlements.note: A beachcomber's hut decorated with ten thousand shells.

settlements.name: Sunder
settlements.note: Fishing town and docks on the warm coast: boats painted bright, nets drying on the dunes.

settlements.name: The stilt village
settlements.note: Houses on stilts joined by rope bridges; everyone poles a boat.

settlements.name: Leech-gatherers' hut
settlements.note: Two sisters who sell leeches to the capital's barbers. Don't ask how they catch them.

settlements.name: Port Sorrow
settlements.note: Rough harbour town where the jungle meets the sea: smugglers, rum, rot.

settlements.name: Turtle beach
settlements.note: A beach camp on a little isle off the Tanglewild.

landmarks.name: The Greyspine
landmarks.note: The great range down the middle of the world, from Embercrown to the Great Inlet. Look closely: it's a spine. The vertebrae are mountains.
landmarks.seen: From almost everywhere in the middle of the world; on the skyline east of Brackenford.

landmarks.name: Embercrown
landmarks.note: A volcano shaped like a skull at the top of the spine, two sockets glowing at night.
landmarks.seen: From the Grey Fells, the Scarrow and the north coast; its glow lights the clouds.

landmarks.name: The Pass
landmarks.note: The one big gap in the Greyspine, between the Witherwood and the Scarrow. A gatehouse and a river at the top.
landmarks.seen: From Ravenscar and the Witherwood's edge.

landmarks.name: The Northwall
landmarks.note: An ancient wall across the Grey Fells, half buried in snow, built against something in the north.
landmarks.seen: From the Witherwood's edge and anywhere high in the north.

landmarks.name: The frozen falls
landmarks.note: A waterfall frozen solid in mid-fall, with a stair cut into it.
landmarks.seen: From the Last Gate on a clear day.

landmarks.name: The Lantern
landmarks.note: A black lighthouse on an island in the Grey Sea. Its light is shuttered: the closed eye.
landmarks.seen: From the Howe Moors' coast; once a year it opens.

landmarks.name: The Bellwood
landmarks.note: Trees in the Witherwood hung with old bells that ring without wind.
landmarks.seen: Heard before seen, from the north road.

landmarks.name: The Ribs
landmarks.note: Stone arches as tall as towers curving out of the desert. Ribshade sits in their shade.
landmarks.seen: From the Elderholt's southern edge and from ships off the south coast.

landmarks.name: The Tailstones
landmarks.note: Rock stacks marching out of the Scour into the sea, like the tail of something.
landmarks.seen: From the Scour's coast and the Sunder lighthouse.

landmarks.name: The Sunk Abbey
landmarks.note: An abbey sinking into the Sump, its tower leaning further every year.
landmarks.seen: From the fen causeway and the Elderholt's edge.

landmarks.name: The Mother Root
landmarks.note: A tree as big as a hill in the Tanglewild, its roots over a ruined city.
landmarks.seen: From the sea and from the Elderholt's western hills.

landmarks.name: The Kittiwake
landmarks.note: A wrecked fishing boat on its side on the shingle, ribs open to the sky. The Wrack's landmark.
landmarks.seen: From the Southbank chantry and the fells above the shore.

act1._about: Act 1 layout sketch v5 (2026-10-21). Positions are [x, z] in metres, same axes as data/world.json: x east, north is -z. Map is 1200 x 1200 m, centred on the origin, cut into 128 m terrain chunks. Heights are rough targets in metres above the river. Draft for Dan; not used by the game yet. v2: enclosed Hollow Lane start, class and profession trainers in Brackenford, Sallow Downs replaces Wolf Ridge as the ruined-farmland zone, a threshold at every zone change, hidden places, a church and a lord's manor. v3: a four-stage opening (Diablo-style intro, RuneScape-style tutors, WoW-style starter zone 1-6, then the world opens). v4 (Dan): required chain is camp, utility belt, then a sealed note to your class trainer, met out in the vale around level 5-6; Mara gives optional errands. v5 (Dan): the starter vale is enclosed like WoW's Northshire, Valley of Trials and Coldridge: one way out (the Neck) to the Crossways, where the world opens. v11 (2026-10-27, Dan: start small like Diablo, Shadowglen, Conquer and Fable, then the world opens): `confined` areas are open only along their roads and pockets (the Hollow Lane, the Neck); `flats` level a town's ground; roads may set their own `corridor`; data/world.json `gates` shut each ring of the opening until its condition holds.

regions.name: Bracken Vale
regions.mood: Warm and safe: hedged fields, a mill, smoke from chimneys, the river always in earshot
regions.biome: River meadows, hedges, farms, the town
regions.enter: You start here. Walled in by the Blackwood Edge, the Beck gill, the Mere carr and the river; the Neck is the only way out.

regions.name: Stillwater
regions.mood: Grey and quiet: mist on the water, a drowned bell, fishers who don't talk much
regions.enter: West from the Crossways along the Mere road, out of the trees to the Staithe on its stilts. Optional in Act 1.

regions.name: Sallow Downs
regions.mood: Gone wrong: burnt farms, empty fields gone to seed, scarecrows, wind, a lord's hall taken by bandits
regions.biome: Bare chalk downs, abandoned farms, gorse
regions.enter: East from the Crossways over Beacon bridge, barred by a Blackhedge toll gate until Act 2. Past it, Blackhedge country: hedged-off commons, burnt farms.

regions.name: The Blackwood
regions.mood: Close and dark: no sky, wet bark, a lit camp you are glad to reach
regions.enter: North from the Crossways through the Wardens' gate; the canopy shuts out the sky. Blackhedge's camp is in here.

regions.name: Hallow Cut
regions.mood: Cold stone and bells: a quarry cut into the hill, wind, a chapel that rings on its own
regions.biome: Stony uplands, quarry gorge, bell chapel
regions.enter: The scarp road from the Downs, past the waterfall. Shut in Act 1.

regions.name: Barrow Fields
regions.mood: Desolate: grey moor, standing stones, grave mounds, no birds
regions.enter: Behind the barrow-mist past the Blackwood. Where the dead stir, much later.

roads.name: Corpse road (through a hidden gully in the Howes)

pois.name: Brackenford
pois.note: Hub town at the ford: the reeve, the inn, the church, Mara's forge and the trade trainers. Waystone. Class trainers live out in the vale. See the town plan.

pois.name: The Last Cart
pois.note: Where the opening ride ends in an ambush and every character wakes, in the sunken Hollow Lane. The iron is gone; a few dropped bars, the manifest, and your bundle with your first weapon and a sealed note for your class trainer.

pois.name: The felled oak
pois.note: Felled across the lane in the ambush, sealing the vale's east side. Later you can clear it from the Downs side: a Fable-style shortcut home.

pois.name: Bracken mill
pois.note: Waterwheel mill; the town's landmark from every road in. The Miller's Wheel quest.

pois.name: Smugglers' cellar (Nell Tallow)
pois.note: Behind the mill wheel; clearing the jammed wheel shows the door. Nell Tallow, the Rogue trainer, works from here; the Rogue's sealed note says how to knock.

pois.name: Hedgecote
pois.note: Farm hamlet: the Ashby/Corrick feud (built), the boundary stone, the old drain. No waystone.

pois.name: Old burying ground
pois.note: Upslope of Hedgecote. Old graves dug into from below: someone is stealing the coffin iron (the feud's true cause).

pois.name: The Old Sough (mine)
pois.note: An old iron mine dug into the Blackwood Edge, levels 5-6. Its sough (drainage tunnel) is the 'old drain' that fouls Hedgecote. Blackhedge's diggers strip iron from the old workings and the burying ground's vault. Gaffer Skell holds some of Mara's stolen bars.

pois.name: The Neck
pois.note: The vale's only way out: a cutting up the Blackwood Edge, kept by Sergeant Brask's wardens. Opens at level 6 after your class trainer's test.

pois.name: The Crossways
pois.note: A signpost at the top of the Neck: west to Stillwater, north into the Blackwood, east to the Downs (barred at Beacon bridge). The world opens here.

pois.name: The Mere's foot
pois.note: The one bit of Mere shore inside the vale: Hester's carp, Tam's sorrel, the ghostfin. The carr beyond is too deep to cross.

pois.name: Beacon bridge
pois.note: Blackhedge's toll gate on the Downs road over Hallow Beck. You can see them from the Crossways; you can't pass until Act 2.

pois.name: Sergeant Brask
pois.note: Warrior trainer, keeping the Neck with his wardens. Meet him around level 5-6 with your note.

pois.name: Fell's lodge
pois.note: Huntsman Odo Fell, the Ranger trainer, at a lodge where the boar runs meet the reeds. Around level 5-6.

pois.name: Mother Grue's hut
pois.note: The Occultist trainer, in a hut above the old burying ground. Around level 5-6.

pois.name: Southbank chantry (Dame Ysolde)
pois.note: Dame Ysolde, the Paladin trainer: the last knight keeping vigil in a half-roofed chantry on the south bank, across the ford. Around level 5-6.

pois.name: The wolf bank
pois.note: Thin hill wolves under the Blackwood Edge, near Odo Fell's lodge. Levels 3-5; skin them for Agna.

pois.name: The boar runs
pois.note: Wild boar; Old Bristleback (rare elite).

pois.name: Gibbet knoll
pois.note: An empty gibbet above the road. The inn's lads bet you won't spend a night under it.

pois.name: Widow Voss's cottage
pois.note: Widow Voss: a broken fence and talk of her son Harl, who went bad. You meet Harl at the end of Act 1, and come back to tell her.

pois.name: The Wardens' gate
pois.note: Palisade on the forest track north of the Crossways. The wardens let through anyone who came up the Neck, with a warning.

pois.name: Washed-out bridge
pois.note: King's Road south. Why caravans now come the long way over the Downs. Gate for a later act.

pois.name: Stillwater Staithe
pois.note: Fishers' hamlet on stilts on the Mere's north-east shore. Old Tam's kin, rod repairs, and boatmen who row something heavy across at night.

pois.name: The drowned chapel
pois.note: A chapel tower standing in the mere. The Drowned Bell tale (hook: the Hallow bells).

pois.name: Dawn stepping-stones
pois.note: Hidden: stones only above water at dawn; the way into the drowned chapel.

pois.name: Reed beds
pois.note: Fen-eels and marsh things at the fen edge.

pois.name: Flooded causeway
pois.note: West to the Mirefen. Gate for a later act.

pois.name: Sallow Bridge
pois.note: Stone bridge over Hallow Beck, reached from the Downs. Across it the lane to town is still blocked by the felled oak until you clear it from this side.

pois.name: Sallow (burnt)
pois.note: Act 2. Burnt hamlet; survivors camp in the barn. Burnt out for refusing to leave.

pois.name: Sallow Hall
pois.note: Act 2. The lord's manor, now Blackhedge's seat. Where the iron goes.

pois.name: Scarecrow fields
pois.note: Fields gone to seed; crows, foxes, something wearing the scarecrows.

pois.name: The old beacon
pois.note: Ruined beacon tower on the ridge, seen from most of the vale.

pois.name: Hermit's hole
pois.note: Hidden: a gap in the gorse below the beacon; a hermit who trades in silver keys.

pois.name: Wardens' watch post
pois.note: Foot of the scarp road. The warden lets you up once Sallow Hall is dealt with.

pois.name: Greyspine rockslide
pois.note: The pass the caravan crossed the night of the opening ride; a rockslide closed it behind you. Gate for a later act.

pois.name: The deadfall
pois.note: Firewood gathering.

pois.name: The Blackhedge camp
pois.note: End of Act 1 (levels 9-10). The gang's woodland camp and lookout rock, the iron stacked under sailcloth. The built bandit chain; Harl Voss, Widow Voss's son, at the end.

pois.name: Woodcutters' camp
pois.note: Lit, fenced forward camp: waystone, trader, a fire. The wood's only safe place.

pois.name: The Old Black
pois.note: A dead giant oak over the canopy, with a face in the bark: a demon door.

pois.name: Where the light ends
pois.note: North of here the wood is too dark to enter without a torch.

pois.name: The wolf den
pois.note: Blackwood wolves.

pois.name: The archers' camp
pois.note: Deserter archers.

pois.name: Trapper's hut
pois.note: The Trapper's Widow (hook: the seer).

pois.name: Hob's ring
pois.note: Hidden: a mushroom ring through a gap in the holly. Dance in it at night (boast).

pois.name: Greyjaw's hollow
pois.note: Old Greyjaw roams here (rare elite).

pois.name: The seer's glade
pois.note: The Blackwood seer: a side tale in Act 1, a bigger part later.

pois.name: Beck falls
pois.note: Hallow Beck drops off the scarp beside the road; you hear it before you see it.

pois.name: Behind the falls
pois.note: Hidden: a cave behind the waterfall with a silver-key chest.

pois.name: Hallow chapel
pois.note: Chapel camp at the top of the scarp: waystone, priest, the bell tower. Later act.

pois.name: The silent watch post
pois.note: Abandoned post; end of the Unpaid Guest tale.

pois.name: Hallow gorge
pois.note: The quarry cut: bog-iron ore, quarry ghouls.

pois.name: Cutters' ruins
pois.note: Ruined quarry village.

pois.name: The barrow-mist
pois.note: Main-path gate: the mist turns you round until the seer's rite. Later act.

pois.name: The Barrow Hollow
pois.note: Restless dead around old mounds.

pois.name: Shepherd's bothy
pois.note: Last roof before the barrow: waystone, a shepherd who counts sheep that aren't there.

pois.name: The Nine Stones
pois.note: Stone ring on the moor edge.

pois.name: The great barrow
pois.note: The mound and its door: the Barrow Below. A later act, where the dead stir (around level 20).

pois.name: East gate
pois.note: Stops you coming in off the lane; sends you to Old Tam to learn to make camp.

pois.name: Wardens' barracks
pois.note: The wardens' barracks. Sergeant Brask is out at the Wardens' gate.

pois.name: Mara's forge
pois.note: Mara Venn: her season's iron was on the cart. Take her the dropped bars (required); optional errands: hooks, a blade. Smithing and Mining trainer.

pois.name: Market square
pois.note: Board quests and bounties; the well.

pois.name: The town well
pois.note: The market well.

pois.name: Reeve's hall
pois.note: Takes the manifest and posts the robbery, issues the utility belt, gives the first job (Hedgecote).

pois.name: North gate
pois.note: The Fallen Road out to Hedgecote, the Mere and the Blackwood.

pois.name: The Ford Inn
pois.note: Hester teaches Cooking. Make it home for rested XP. The Ford Stone sits in the yard.

pois.name: The ford
pois.note: Teaches Set Camp (required) and Fishing.

pois.name: St Wenna's church
pois.note: Churchyard and Sexton Harrow, who keeps the burying ground and is upset about the graves.

pois.name: Bracken mill
pois.note: Landmark. The smugglers' cellar behind the wheel is the Rogue trainer's.

pois.name: Agna's tannery
pois.note: Skinning trainer, downstream for the smell.

tutorial.text: Dawn in the sunken lane. Learn to move and look.
The iron is gone. The manifest, a few dropped bars, and your bundle: first weapon and a sealed note.
Crows and a hungry fox at the bodies.
Your respawn point until you can make camp.
Warden Tobin lets you in and sends you to Old Tam.
Required: hand in the manifest, get the utility belt.
Required: the dropped bars. Optional errands: hooks, a blade.

path.name: The Last Cart: the iron is stolen
Brackenford: camp, the belt, Mara's dropped bars
Bracken Vale: farms, boar, wolves, trades, your trainer
The Old Sough: Mara's bars, Skell's tally
Up the Neck into the Blackwood
The Blackhedge camp and Harl Voss: end of Act 1

legs.name: Last Cart to Brackenford's east gate
Brackenford north gate to the Neck
Woodcutters' camp to the seer's glade

gatesInAct1: North gate (level 3): the warden keeps strangers in town until Reeve Pell gives you your first job.
The Neck (level 6): the vale's only way out, opened by Sergeant Brask after your class trainer's test.
Torchlight: the deep Blackwood past the Woodcutters' camp needs a torch.
Beacon bridge toll gate: Blackhedge hold the Downs road. Opens in Act 2.
Felled oak: seals the vale's east side; cleared from the Downs side in Act 2 as a shortcut home.
Scarp road and barrow-mist: shut for later acts.

opening.name: The Last Cart
opening.where: Sallow road at night, then the Hollow Lane
opening.summary: One path forward, told like a story. You can't get lost or wander off.
beats: Night, riding the cart down from the Greyspine pass, over Sallow Bridge. The carter talks: the cart carries a season's bar iron for the Brackenford smith, the dearest load on the road. Your class is one line of who you are. Skippable.

Ambush in the Hollow Lane: men with blackthorn sprigs in their hats, an oak crashes down behind. Two of them fight you with prompts for attacking and your first ability, then go back to loading the iron.

Black out. Wake at dawn among the dead. The iron is gone. Loot the wreck: the manifest, a few bars they dropped, and your own bundle with your first weapon and a sealed note from your old master to your class trainer. Equip it.
Follow the lane: crows and a hungry fox at the bodies. Nobody comes looking for a caravan hand; you are on your own.
The lane shrine sets your respawn. Warden Tobin lets you in at the east gate: no beds for strangers without coin, so go and see Old Tam.

opening.name: Brackenford
opening.where: Brackenford; the north gate stays shut until the reeve says
opening.summary: Two things are required, the rest is offered, never forced. Each person points you to the next.
beats: Required: Old Tam at the ford teaches Set Camp. Your camp is your respawn and your rested XP from now on.
Required: Reeve Pell takes the manifest and posts the robbery. He issues you a wardens' utility belt for tools, torch and rod: the town is short of hands and you are one.

Required: take the dropped bars to Mara Venn. Her whole season's iron was on that cart. She can't do much with four bars, but she sharpens your weapon and asks you to keep an eye out. Optional: she has hooks for Old Tam and a blade for Agna; carry them and each teaches you their trade (Fishing, Skinning). Mara herself teaches Mining and Smithing.
Optional: Hester teaches Cooking; make the inn your home.
Reeve Pell's first job: trouble at Hedgecote. Level 3; the north gate opens.

opening.name: Bracken Vale
opening.where: The whole south of the map
opening.summary: An enclosed valley like Northshire or Coldridge: the Blackwood Edge to the north, the Beck gill to the east, the Mere carr to the west, the river and downs to the south. About 25 quests, most already built.
beats: Two hubs, Brackenford and Hedgecote, with the trainers' homes tucked into the vale's corners.

Built already: the Ashby/Corrick feud and Wren and Cal's secret love, Hester's fish, Agna's hides and the board bounties. The boar are worked up and wrecking the fields: thin them, and Old Bristleback.
Wolves under the Edge, thinned for their pelts. Small tales: the Ford Stone, a dare at the empty gibbet, the miller's jammed wheel, Widow Voss's fence.

The Old Sough (levels 5-6): the farm stories end here. Cal's shilling-a-night sacks, Bram's pigs and the fouled drain all lead to the old mine, where Blackhedge's diggers strip iron from the old workings and the burying vault. The elite Gaffer Skell has some of Mara's marked bars in his strongbox. Bring them home and Mara forges you a proper weapon.

Required, around level 5-6: hand your sealed note to your class trainer, out at the vale's edge: Brask at the Neck, Odo Fell at his lodge by the reeds, Nell Tallow in the smugglers' cellar, Mother Grue above the burying ground, Dame Ysolde (Paladin) at the chantry across the ford. Their test of might is the graduation, and Brask lets you up the Neck. Level 6.

opening.name: The bandit trail
opening.inspired: Fable 1's Bower Lake bandits, RuneScape's open world
opening.where: Up the Neck into the Blackwood; Stillwater on the side
opening.summary: One way out, then a trail to follow. Skell's tally says the rest of the iron went up the Neck to Blackhedge's camp in the wood.
beats: Up the Neck past Brask's wardens to the Crossways. East, the Downs road is barred at Beacon bridge by a Blackhedge toll gate: you can see the enemy holds the road, but not yet.
North through the Wardens' gate to the Woodcutters' camp: wolves, deserters, Old Greyjaw, wood that needs a torch.
West along the Mere road (optional): Stillwater's boatmen have been ferrying something heavy across the mere at night.
The Blackhedge camp (levels 9-10): the built bandit chain, cut-throats and bowmen, and Harl Voss, Widow Voss's son. Spare him or don't, then tell his mother.
Harl's papers: the iron goes east over Beacon bridge to Sallow Hall, and the downs beyond are Blackhedge country now. End of Act 1; Act 2 opens the Downs.

act1.laterQuests: The Missing Delivery is reworked into the manifest (Reeve Pell, the belt) and Mara's Iron. Moved up to 6-10 on the bandit trail: the bandit chain (bandit_rag, scout, thin, captain) and Harl Voss, the Wolf Den and Greyjaw in the Blackwood. dungeon.name: The Old Sough
dungeon.why: A confined test before the vale lets you out: narrow tunnels, careful pulls, a dark stretch, one telegraphed elite.
dungeon.story: The 'old drain' in the feud is this mine's sough. Blackhedge's diggers strip iron from the old workings and break into the burying vault for coffin iron. Cal hauled the sacks out of the sough mouth for a shilling a night. Bram's pigs are penned at their hut.

rooms.name: Sough mouth
rooms.note: The culvert where the drain runs out at the foot of the Edge. Boot prints and a dropped sack (examine).

rooms.name: The adit
rooms.note: A low, narrow tunnel. Mine rats in twos: teaches pulling one group at a time.

rooms.name: Gin-pit chamber
rooms.note: Old winding gear. Three diggers (level 5) and one patrol walking the loop.

rooms.name: Flooded gallery
rooms.note: Knee-deep and pitch dark: light your torch from the utility belt. Slow wading; things in the water.

rooms.name: The fall
rooms.note: Optional side working. A cave-in trap with a ground telegraph (practice dodging) and a silver-key cache behind the rubble.

rooms.name: The breakthrough
rooms.note: A rough hole into the burying vault: sacks of coffin iron. The 'What Lies Under' objective.

rooms.name: The burying vault

elite.name: Gaffer Skell
elite.what: Blackhedge's digger, a big man with a mattock and a hooded lamp.
moves: Mattock sweep: a frontal cone telegraph. Step out of it.
Lamp oil: throws a burning pool (circle telegraph) that stays for a few seconds.
At half health he calls two mine rats out of the walls.
No stuns (he fills the stagger bar like a boss); a good first test of the telegraph rules.

chest.name: Skell's strongbox
chest.what: Six of Mara's marked bars from the cart, silver, and Skell's tally: the rest of the iron went up the Neck to the camp in the wood. Mara turns the bars into an uncommon weapon for your class.

review.title: Act 1 story: grounded, ending on the bandit trail
review.verdict: Act 1 now follows your flow: the cart is robbed, Mara's iron is gone, and everything a nobody does in the vale (farms, boar, wolves, trades, the trainer) quietly points at the same thieves. The farm stories lead into the mine, the mine leads up the Neck, and Act 1 ends at Blackhedge's camp with the trail running east into the Downs for Act 2. No undead, no prophecy, no chosen one.

flow.x: Blackthorn sprigs in their hats. The iron is the prize.
Camp (Tam), the belt (Pell), the dropped bars (Mara). Fishing, Cooking, Skinning if you like.
The feud and the secret love, worked-up boar, wolves for pelts, Bram's pigs.
The sealed note, a test of might, around level 5-6.
The drain, Cal's sacks and the pigs all lead to the Old Sough. Mara's bars come home and become your weapon.
Up the Neck, the Blackwood, the Blackhedge camp, Harl Voss. Act 1 ends at level 10.
Over Beacon bridge into the Downs: how Blackhedge took the land.

ladder.stories: Chores, errands, the feud, boar and wolves, thieves in a mine. Every problem is solved by the end of its quest.
The same thieves, followed home: a camp in the wood and a local man gone bad. Act 1 ends here.
Who Blackhedge work for and how they took the land. One letter with a closed-eye seal, never explained yet.
The dead under the barrows (around level 20), the closed eye, the wider world.

bandits.title: Who are Blackhedge? Not the Defias
bandits.pick: Hedgers: hired muscle for a land grab
bandits.text: The Defias are wronged workers taking revenge on the crown. Blackhedge are the opposite: men paid to take land from farmers. With the lord away, someone has bought up the commons on the Sallow Downs for sheep. Blackhedge are the crews who hedge them off, burn out anyone who won't go, and hold the gaps. Iron is scarce and they need a lot of it for blades and fence stakes, so they steal it: the cart, the old mine, the graves. Their mark is a blackthorn sprig. In Act 1 you only see the bottom of it (thieves, diggers, a camp). In Act 2 the 'wasteland' is the enclosed downs: hedges where villages were, sheep in the burnt fields. It's grounded in real English history, and the farm feud over a hedge and a boundary stone already fits it.
others: Toll-keepers: they have quietly replaced the absent lord and charge 'the lord's toll' on every road. Some villages prefer them. Morally grey, but less tied to the land.
Plain bandits with a bandit king, like Fable's Twinblade: the simplest, and the least our own.

beyond.what: The Greyspine mountains: snow peaks on the skyline from the Crossways. The pass you came over, now shut by a rockslide.
The King's Road to the capital (name to pick). The washed-out bridge.
The Mirefen: fen smoke and marsh lights on the horizon from Stillwater, past the flooded causeway.
The beacon chain: the Downs beacon is one of a line of dead beacons running north to an old border. From the Barrow Fields you can see the next one, far off.
